worked_solution:
We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{10}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x & =10{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-1}{x}^{-6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =10{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{-5}]}_{a}^{-1} \\  & =-2\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{{x}^{5}}]}_{a}^{-1} \\  & =-2\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-1)^{5}}-\frac{1}{{a}^{5}}] \\  & =-2\cdot (-1-0) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
